items.q: What limits local, interactively prompted coding agents?
items.a: They are capped by **human throughput** and can't be automated, and everyone's own setup makes **cost, productivity and security** hard to govern.

items.q: How does Zach Lloyd define a software factory?
items.a: A **code-defined closed loop** for **continuously measuring and improving** cloud coding agents.
Agents, triggers, workflows, MCPs and policies in **Terraform-style declarative files**, so you can **branch, test and roll back** the factory.

items.q: Why record every agent conversation and artifact?
items.a: It is the **raw material for improving** the factory over time.

items.q: How should a factory treat models and harnesses?
items.a: As **degrees of freedom to test**: support several models and coding agents.

items.q: What is an online eval for coding agents?
items.a: Another agent **scores every session** on a dimension, such as catching **redundant tests**.
Agents find patterns in failed runs and propose fixes as **PRs against the factory definition**.

items.q: How do you know which model or skill is best?
items.a: **Replay your own real tasks** against configurations and compare **cost versus quality**.
